assessment: The only production delta adds a fast path after the existing NSNumber and CFBoolean checks. Exact one-character signed c/s/i/l/q encodings use int64_t longLongValue and reject negative values; exact unsigned C/S/I/L/Q encodings use uint64_t unsignedLongLongValue. Each retains the positive-versus-zero policy without a floating-point conversion, including UINT64_MAX.

Decimal, floating and unknown/multichar encodings still execute the byte-identical digit-string fallback, including its 20-digit and UINT64_MAX comparison. Class refusal, boolean refusal, schema validation-before-retained-mutation, thread/callback behavior and ownership are unchanged.

The added boundary matrix exercises the actual NSJSONSerialization validation path for generation and the three grid integer fields: zero/positive policies, signed-width boundaries, 2^53, signed/unsigned 64-bit boundaries, negative/fractional/oversized/boolean/non-number rejection. It establishes expected parsed-JSON behavior; it does not force every possible custom NSNumber subclass or objcType.

The microbenchmark uses one host, 50 rows and 400 cells (451 total nodes), prevalidates the immutable payload, and times repeated production native validation. It is a native validation diagnostic, not a rendered-frame or P6 workload benchmark.
limits: Read/hash/diff-only review of exactly two candidate leaves. No reviewer tests, builds, native/UI calls, provider runs, Git actions or source edits.
Author original/candidate boundary and race receipts were not independently executed or evidence-qualified by this source review.

No latency, whole-frame/total-UI-work, native memory, physical GPU or broad Mac/P6 acceptance claim. The native main-thread asynchronous validation path may lie outside the existing exact totalUI accounting.
